name: PW-1-the-hasher-takes-an-empty-credential-again
old: if (!normalise(pw)) throw new Error('refusing to hash an empty credential - a caller handed this null or ""');
note: The exact state the Q fold shipped in: a minted code that does not canonicalise hashes the EMPTY STRING into recovery_hash, and `recover`'s own `canon ?? ''` then opens that account with any string that is not a code.

name: PW-2-the-constant-time-compare-fails-open-again
old:
if (!(a instanceof Uint8Array) || !(b instanceof Uint8Array)) return false;
  const x = a; const y = b;
new:
const x = a instanceof Uint8Array ? a : new Uint8Array(0);
  const y = b instanceof Uint8Array ? b : new Uint8Array(0);
note: The coercion this audit removed. timingSafeEqual(null, null) answers TRUE - a defensive default that defends in the wrong direction, on the one primitive that must never guess.

name: PW-3-the-folding-eats-a-letter-the-alphabet-contains
note: THE RECORDED BUG, restored. Q is IN the alphabet, so folding it makes a minted code canonicalise to a different string than the one that was hashed - and with PW-1's refusal in place it is now a loud 500 at registration rather than a silent skeleton key.

name: PW-4-verify-short-circuits-before-the-derivation
old:
const got = await derive(pw, salt, iters, subtle);
  if (!parsed) return false;
new:
if (!parsed) return false;
  const got = await derive(pw, salt, iters, subtle);
note: "This account has no password" then costs nothing and "this password is wrong" costs 210,000 iterations - which is a username oracle on the clock, the exact thing login's own comment says it is paying for.

name: PW-5-the-length-is-not-part-of-the-compare
note: With the modulo indexing below, a short array that repeats into a longer one compares EQUAL - the length is the only thing that stops it.

name: PW-6-the-code-alphabet-stops-being-a-power-of-two
note: 33 characters masked with 32 is a biased draw over a 100-bit secret. The minter throws rather than drawing it, which is the guard the file writes out loud - this checks the guard is reachable and that the alphabet pin notices.
